[0] The current government's term has less than a year remaining. After Legislative Council members concluded their Beijing "study and exchange" trip, Chief Executive John Lee held his first "exchange meeting" today (28th). The closed-door meeting was held in the Legislative Council banquet hall and lasted approximately 1.5 hours. After the meeting, John Lee and Legislative Council Chairman Andrew Leung met the press. Lee stated that he had an "in-depth and constructive" exchange with 67 members without any restrictions, and that this consolidated the consensus of being "Team Hong Kong members." Lee also pointed out that the executive and legislature are "people in the same boat," and that the Legislative Council, as the government's governing partner, jointly promotes reform, meaning "we are all Team Hong Kong members."

[1] Chief Executive John Lee and Legislative Council Chairman Andrew Leung meet the press after the exchange meeting.

[2] Chief Executive John Lee and Legislative Council Chairman Andrew Leung meet reporters after the exchange meeting. Lee stated that he had an in-depth and constructive exchange with 67 members, deepening mutual understanding, bringing them closer, and sharing his thoughts on "patriots governing Hong Kong." He described the Legislative Council as the government's reform partner, pointing out that both the executive and legislature share the goal of solving problems for citizens. Through exchange and dialogue, different perspectives can be connected, mutual understanding achieved, and supervision and cooperation balanced, helping the executive and legislature to build consensus and focus more on getting things done.

[3] Lee added that under executive-led governance, he constantly contemplates how to continuously create new value for "patriots governing Hong Kong," and this exchange meeting is one such innovative initiative. In a relaxed environment without procedural constraints, "the Chief Executive and members conversed like Team Hong Kong members," unrestricted, allowing for in-depth and constructive exchanges on issues. The exchanges were not limited to one-on-one dialogues; multiple members could engage in in-depth discussions on the same topic simultaneously, sharing their thoughts and feelings, adding a human touch to communication.

[4] Lee stated that, without any procedural constraints, he had in-depth and constructive exchanges with members.

[5] Lee also spoke at length about his vision for "patriots governing Hong Kong," pointing out that the reform process would touch on many vested interests, making implementation difficult. He said the executive and legislature must properly handle systemic relationships—micro and macro, overall and partial, current and long-term, special and general, primary and secondary—to achieve a high degree of consensus and produce results. He described today's exchange as positive and constructive, and said there would be a review to see if there is room for improvement. He also stated that he had listened to members sharing their observations from the Beijing study trip, and considered the national policies and their implementation worth emulating.

[6] Andrew Leung said the exchange meeting was very successful, and one outcome was that a member, inspired by Beijing's 12345 hotline, proposed visiting the 1823 government hotline, which the Chief Executive had noted and agreed to.

[7] Andrew Leung: Very successful, talked about everything

[8] Andrew Leung described the exchange meeting as very successful, with 15 members sharing their views and speaking, including sharing their observations from last week's Beijing study and exchange trip, achieving "truly broad discussion." She said the executive and legislature are "people in the same boat," and the Legislative Council, as the government's governing partner, jointly promotes reform, meaning "we are all Team Hong Kong members." She expressed confidence that as long as the executive and legislature continue to maintain positive interaction and efficient collaboration through different channels, put people first, and draw on the country's successful experience, they can better solve problems for citizens.

[9] She also pointed out that the 15 members who spoke shared "the outcomes of the Beijing study trip." Some members had previously visited the Beijing 12345 citizen service hotline center. Citing the example of a member suggesting visiting the local 1823 hotline to learn how to better serve the public, she said the Chief Executive had noted and agreed to members visiting the 1823 hotline.

[10] The current government has introduced a number of measures claimed to help improve executive-legislative relations, including the establishment of the "Pre-function Exchange Meeting" to allow officials and members to exchange views on policies, and the change of the Chief Executive's Question Time to an "Interactive Exchange Q&A Session." The Administration Wing recently wrote to the Legislative Council stating that the exchange meeting aimed to allow everyone to engage in "in-depth and constructive direct exchanges" in a relaxed environment. At the meeting, the Chief Executive first shared his practical experience and thoughts on "patriots governing Hong Kong," followed by an unrestricted open dialogue covering topics that could include national, Hong Kong, and even international affairs, with flexible content.
